newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore stock market volume reaches 1993 levels.
newsitem.headline: Singapore stock market volume reaches 1993 levels.

text.p: A feverish pace of trade on the Singapore bourse pushed turnover to near record levels on Thursday, stock exchange dealers said.
The volume seen today was similar to that achieved in the super bullish year of 1993, they said.
Today's volume was a hefty 771.82 million shares, according to the Stock Exchange of Singapore (SES). The volume includes foreign currency denominated stocks.
The volume for Singapore dollar denominated stocks, which includes Malaysian stocks traded over-the-counter, was 746.91 million shares worth Singapore $1.27 billion.

The benchmark Straits Times index ended up 1.35 percent, by 30.04 points to 2,254.68. A SES official said the all-time record in volume terms for Singapore dollar denominated stocks on the local bourse was 770.07 million shares worth S$1.62 billion achieved on December 29, 1993.
Trading activity on the Singapore market also continued to outstrip the volume on the neighbouring Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange (KLSE) for the second consecutive day.
Volume on the KLSE was 589.14 million units worth 2.79 billion ringgit on Thursday.

Stephen Loh, head of institutional sales, at DBS Securities, said: "I think this is genuine foreign fund inflow who are adjusting their portfolios. They are re-rating Singapore as the economic numbers look a bit better."
Singapore said last week the economy grew by seven percent in 1996, up from the previous official estimate of 6.5 percent.

Another dealer said there could some fund flows out of Hong Kong into Singapore. "Hong Kong ended sharply lower in the afternoon on rumours of Deng's heath. There was some nervousness here too at first but the market was able to take it in stride."
But Loh said he was not convinced today was the start of a bull run similar to that seen in 1993.
"At this stage I don't think it is a bull run type of scenario. The volume seen today of over S$1.2 billion can be repeated a few more times as the sentiment is there to propel it," he said.
Dealers noted there was a lot of inter-market trading between Singapore and Malaysia, mainly arbitrage activity between the two markets.
More than half of the volume in Singapore was generated by Malaysian OTC stocks.
The UOB-OTC index jumped over 20 points to a record of 1,343.09 before a sell-off in the late afternoon eroded all gains. The index ended down 9.40 points at 1,313.10.
